title: From Bollywood to the New York Stage: Jay Patel Co-Produces The Flowers of Forest Hills
excerpt: The immigration drama by Claude Solnik premieres November 5 at Theater for the New City, following three generations of women building a life in Forest Hills.
body:
• Indian-American producer Jay Patel has co-produced The Flowers of Forest Hills, which premieres November 5 and runs through November 22 at Theater for the New City in Manhattan.
  • The two-act play by Claude Solnik, directed by Patricia Magno, follows three generations of women in a family that emigrated to America and built a new life in Forest Hills.
  • Patel, a Bollywood producer who has called New York home for more than three decades, says he sees the immigration story as film-worthy.
  • Tickets and run details are carried in BroadwayWorld's listing for the production.

Bollywood producer Jay Patel has brought an immigration story to the New York stage. The Flowers of Forest Hills premieres November 5 and runs through November 22 at Theater for the New City in Manhattan, presented by Executive Artistic Director Crystal Field, according to BroadwayWorld.

The play, by playwright and journalist Claude Solnik and directed by Patricia Magno, is based on a true story about emigrating to America in a time of global upheaval. It follows a family that creates a new life in America and lives with the compromises that success required, centred on three generations of women.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=zo2GjXGFIVk

"Art preserves what time tries to erase. The beauty of art is that one person's story can become the story of billions."

— Jay Patel, producer

An Immigration Story, Told Straight

"It's really an immigration story," Solnik said. "It's very much based on true events and how in order to adapt and succeed in America, people sometimes make decisions that create difficulties later." Magno described it as "a story about belonging, the fact that we all belong to a society, a family, or simply to each other."

Doriana Schoner plays Sylvie, who grows from a baby in a carriage marked with a Jewish star in Austria into an enterprising young woman in Forest Hills, caught between adoptive and real parents as the family launches a successful business. The cast also includes Gail Merzer Behrens, Mike Cesarano, Noah Frankenfield, Karen Freer, Jon Lonoff and Carolyn Seiff, Sunvilla Samachar reported.

Patel's Longer Arc

Patel is an Indian-American entrepreneur, actor, film producer and author who has lived in New York for more than three decades. "Theatre is one of the most beautiful ways to bring people together, through stories, emotions and shared experiences," he said. He describes the production as the start of a longer creative partnership with Solnik, and has said he sees the story as film-worthy.

How to See It

The Flowers of Forest Hills runs November 5-22 at Theater for the New City in Manhattan, in a two-act production just under two hours. Run and ticket details are in the BroadwayWorld listing.

The Production Team

Crystal Field presents the production for Theater for the New City. Cameron Reilly-Steele serves as assistant director, with Marsh Shugart on sound and light design and Reuben Speed on set design, Sunvilla Samachar reported. For Patel, who has worked across film production and acting, the run is also a statement about where diaspora producers are putting work: not only into cinema, but into live New York theatre telling migration stories to the city that receives the migrants.
